input.title: Critical RCE in Fortinet FortiGate exploited in the wild, patch now
input.body: Fortinet has confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-31337, a pre-auth remote code execution flaw in FortiGate appliances. Attackers are deploying webshells on unpatched devices. A fix is available in FortiOS 7.6.4.

input.title: Top 10 cybersecurity certifications to boost your career in 2026
input.body: Thinking about a career move? Here are the certifications hiring managers love, from CISSP to OSCP, and what they cost.

input.title: Ransomware gang leaks 2TB of data stolen from European hospital group
input.body: The Qilin ransomware group published data allegedly exfiltrated from a hospital network spanning three EU countries after ransom negotiations collapsed. Patient records appear to be included, regulators have been notified.

input.title: Why zero trust is more than a buzzword: an opinion
input.body: In this op-ed, our contributor argues that zero trust architectures are misunderstood and that vendors have diluted the term. He offers his view of what practitioners should focus on instead.

input.title: Acme Security launches AI-powered SOC platform with 40% off launch pricing
input.body: Acme Security today announced the general availability of its next-gen SOC platform featuring AI triage. Early customers get discounted pricing through the end of the quarter. Book a demo today.

input.title: Supply-chain attack on npm package 'httpkit' backdoors 4M weekly downloads
input.body: A maintainer account compromise led to malicious versions of httpkit being published for six hours. The payload exfiltrates environment variables to an attacker-controlled server. Versions 3.2.1-3.2.3 are affected; the registry has removed them.

input.title: How to set up your first home lab for malware analysis
input.body: A step-by-step tutorial covering VM isolation, snapshotting, REMnux, and safe sample handling for beginners who want to learn reverse engineering.

input.title: CISA orders federal agencies to patch actively exploited Chrome zero-day
input.body: CISA added CVE-2026-2882, a V8 type-confusion bug exploited in targeted campaigns, to the KEV catalog and set a 7-day remediation deadline for federal civilian agencies. Google shipped a fix in Chrome 138.

input.title: Infosec conference season: our picks for 2026
input.body: From RSA to DEF CON, here are the talks and villages we're most excited about this year, plus travel tips for first-time attendees.

input.title: Microsoft: Chinese state actor breached government email via token forgery
input.body: Microsoft disclosed that a threat actor it tracks as Storm-0558 forged authentication tokens using an acquired signing key to access email accounts at multiple government agencies. Microsoft has revoked the key and published IOCs.

input.title: Bank of Meridian reports quarterly earnings beat, shares rise 4%
input.body: The regional bank posted better-than-expected earnings driven by loan growth. Executives cited stable deposit trends and reiterated full-year guidance.

input.title: Data breach at retailer LoomMart exposes 8.4 million customer records
input.body: LoomMart confirmed attackers accessed a customer database containing names, emails, hashed passwords, and partial payment data. The company is notifying affected customers and offering credit monitoring. The intrusion began through a compromised vendor account.

input.title: 5 password managers we recommend this year
input.body: Our annual roundup compares features, pricing, and security track records of popular password managers to help you pick one.

input.title: PoC exploit released for critical Jenkins CLI file-read vulnerability
input.body: Security researchers published a proof-of-concept for CVE-2026-20991, which lets unauthenticated attackers read arbitrary files on Jenkins controllers. Shadowserver observes scanning activity. Administrators should update to the patched LTS release.

input.title: What is SBOM and why should you care? A primer
input.body: This explainer covers software bills of materials, the regulatory push behind them, and how organizations use them for supply-chain risk management.

input.title: DDoS attack takes Estonian government portals offline for six hours
input.body: A politically motivated hacktivist group claimed a volumetric DDoS attack that disrupted access to several Estonian e-government services. Officials say no data was compromised and services were restored with upstream filtering.

input.title: Passwordless authentication adoption grows among enterprises, survey finds
input.body: A vendor-sponsored survey of 500 IT leaders found 61% plan to expand passkey deployments next year, citing phishing resistance and support costs.

input.title: VMware ESXi hypervisor flaw allows sandbox escape, patches released
input.body: Broadcom released fixes for CVE-2026-22945, a use-after-free in ESXi's USB controller emulation that allows a VM escape. The flaw was demonstrated at Pwn2Own and affects ESXi 8.x and 7.x.

input.title: Sports team announces new stadium naming deal with tech company
input.body: The 10-year naming-rights agreement is reportedly worth $300 million and includes technology integrations across the venue.

input.title: Okta warns of credential-stuffing wave targeting customer identity endpoints
input.body: Okta observed a spike in credential-stuffing attacks against customer identity cloud endpoints originating from residential proxies, and recommends enabling breached-password detection and rate limits.
